messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired — SERVICE: global-rate-limiter — ALERT: RATE_LIMIT_QUOTA_ANOMALY. Spike in 429s starting ~06:09 UTC. Affected: tenant-47, tenant-12, tenant-99. PD: https://pd.example/incidents/PD12345. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/rl-quota-anomaly. Please acknowledge and follow on-call playbook.

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification: sent to SRE Rotation (primary). Escalation timer: 5m. Incident ID: PD12345.

Alex C: ack — I'm oncall. Pulling dashboards and logs now. Any immediate customer reports? @Maria G, can you check CS slack? :eyes: 

Maria G: CS: no inbound tickets yet but we have telemetry alerting in datadog — dash link: https://dd.example/org/rl/alerts/7432. 429s jump from baseline ~0.2% to 7% overall, started 06:08. Latency p95 ok. Looks like enforcement spike rather than perf.

Devin R: quick glance at limiter logs on rl-4: `segfault at 0x0` around 06:08 then process restart. On restart, quota-mapper returns 500/deny for many tenants: `quota-mapper: mapping not found -> deny`. Repro command I ran: `kubectl exec -n infra rl-proxy-rl-4 -- curl -v http://localhost:8080/tenant/47/allow` shows 429.

Ken T: If quota-mapper state is lost after a crash it can default to deny. Workaround: flip `rl.migration.safe_mode=true` to make mapper fall back to permissive routing, or route to fallback-limiter. I'll prepare a canary change (10% traffic).

Alex C: Do the canary. I'll monitor. Command I'm running: `kubectl set env deploy/rl-proxy CANARY=enabled --namespace=prod --record` -> will move 10% via klot controller.

Ops Bot: Canary rollout started for deployment/rl-proxy. New pods: rl-proxy-canary-1, rl-proxy-canary-2. Healthchecks OK.

Maria G: Early signals: tenants on canary show 429s drop to ~0.3%. Aggregate 429 rate down ~60% since canary. Good sign.

Devin R: Opening PD incident as P1 (already paged but elevating severity). PD link updated with mitigation steps and logs: PD12345-1. Attaching `rl-4` logs and stack traces.

Alex C: Notifying CS & Account teams. @Maria G can you compile a short impacted-customers list and we can draft outbound? Need to know any high-importance tenants.

Maria G: Quick tally: ~12 tenants saw >5% failures last 20m; 3 tenants >20% (tenant-12, tenant-47, tenant-99). DMing CS with contact list and suggested message.

SRE Rotation: If canary stable for 10m, recommend rolling mitigation cluster-wide then proceed to rollback the offending quota-mapper deploy (last prod deploy at 2026-03-14T05:58Z).

Ken T: Preliminary root cause: memory leak in quota-mapper triggered by high sync rate after the 05:58 deploy; led to process crash and missing mappings on restart. I'll prepare rollback and heap dumps.

Alex C: Rolling back quota-mapper: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/quota-mapper -n infra --to-revision=42` — triggering now.

Ops Bot: Rollback initiated for deployment/quota-mapper. New pods coming up, old pods terminating.

Maria G: Post-rollback metrics are trending back to baseline. 429s returned to ~0.2% across tenants. Affected tenants showing successful requests again.

Devin R: Collecting heapdumps and core from rl-4 and quota-mapper for postmortem: `gcore` + `/var/log/rl/quota-mapper.log` attached to PD. Will schedule deep-dive.

Alex C: Good job team. Keep PD updated, CS notified, and let's keep monitoring for 30m. I'll stay on until handoff.

SRE Rotation: Acknowledged. I'll take handoff at 07:00 UTC and continue monitoring. Please add timeline and mitigation commands to PD.

incident-bot: Incident PD12345 marked mitigated — mitigation applied (canary + rollback), service returning to normal. Postmortem owner: Devin R. Next steps: follow-up postmortem, deploy fix for memory leak, add stronger liveness/health checks for quota-mapper.

Alex C: Closing thread for now — will reopen if regression. Thanks everyone :tada:
